chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abdul Aziz ibn al-Muhtadi, from his grandfather, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Sa'd ibn Sa'd, that he said:

I asked him, meaning Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him), about a man who had a son whom he acknowledged, but then disowned him and excluded him from the inheritance, while I am his executor. So what should I do? He (peace be upon him) said: The son is bound by his acknowledgment in public; the executor cannot repel him from anything that is known.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on an adopted son who is disowned by his father regarding inheritance?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) establishes that a father's public acknowledgment (iqrar) of a son creates a binding legal relationship that the executor (wasi) cannot unilaterally sever to exclude the son from inheritance. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle that the father's voluntary declaration holds evidentiary weight sufficient to maintain the son's status, even if he is subsequently 'disowned' or removed from the household, provided the acknowledgment was clear and witnessed.
